ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary sinus

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital mass with exophthalmia, hemifacial pain, and visual impairment
salient_findings: Left exophthalmia with vision impairment and complete restriction of ocular motility
Medial bulging of the left nasal fossa lateral wall and leftward septal deviation
Soft-tissue density lesion occupying the left maxillary sinus with extension into the orbit and sinuses
key_facts: 65-year-old woman
5-month history of progressive orbital mass
Poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 8 years
History of stage IIB cervical adenocarcinoma treated with radiotherapy and cisplatin
Well-controlled hypertension, dyslipidemia, and hypothyroidism
Left exophthalmia with vision impairment and complete restriction of ocular motility
Medial bulging of the left nasal fossa lateral wall and leftward septal deviation
Contrast-enhanced CT showed soft-tissue density lesion in the left maxillary sinus
MRI demonstrated heterogeneously enhancing mass in the left maxillary sinus and orbit
Bone disruption of the lateral and inferior orbital walls
Extension through the inferior orbital fissure and invasion of the left cavernous sinus
Diffusion restriction around the ophthalmic nerve
Anterior displacement of the extraocular muscles and vessels
HbA1c 8.8%
CRP 15.5 mg/L
ESR 120 mm/h
Positive anti-HBc

shortlist: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary sinus

shortlist.label: Sinonasal lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy revealed probable low-grade lymphoproliferative lesion

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary sinus
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive features on imaging, such as bone disruption and invasion of the cavernous sinus

shortlist.label: Esthesioneuroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive orbital mass with exophthalmia and visual impairment, suggestive of an aggressive sinonasal tumor

shortlist.label: Sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression and aggressive features on imaging, consistent with a highly malignant tumor

shortlist.label: Mucormycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Poorly controlled diabetes mellitus and history of immunosuppression, increasing the risk of invasive fungal infection

raw.rationale: The patient's biopsy results showed a probable low-grade lymphoproliferative lesion, which is consistent with sinonasal lymphoma. The patient's history of cervical adenocarcinoma and treatment with radiotherapy and cisplatin may also increase the risk of developing lymphoma.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary sinus
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of smoking and radiation exposure, the biopsy results do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Esthesioneuroblastoma
rejected.why: The patient's age and presentation are not typical for esthesioneuroblastoma, and the biopsy results do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma
rejected.why: The biopsy results do not support this diagnosis, and the patient's presentation is more consistent with a lymphoproliferative disorder

rejected.label: Mucormycosis
rejected.why: The patient's laboratory results, including negative Cryptococcus antigen and nonreactive FTA-ABS, do not support a diagnosis of mucormycosis
